title: Release train coordination for runtime-1.21 (tiered batching): branch cut, backports, CI stability, release notes checklist
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
## Summary
Coordinate runtime-1.21 release train changes required for Workload-aware batching defaults (fast/standard/cost-efficient tiers).

This ticket is the release-engineering umbrella for:
- Branch cut timing + freeze rules
- Backport policy (what qualifies, how to validate)
- CI/perf-canary stability plan
- Release notes checklist (runtime + docs + console-facing artifacts)

## Context
Tiered batching touches scheduler behavior + metrics + config schema. We need a predictable release process because tail-latency regressions and perf-canary flakes were observed during development (notably streaming cadence + queue delay sensitivity).

Key workstreams landing in/around 1.21:
- Config schema: `batching_tier` (fast/standard/cost_efficient) + precedence over explicit knobs (explicit overrides win)
- Runtime tier mapping + workload-signal driven selection (prompt length buckets, concurrency, streaming)
- New metrics: queue delay + batch formation histograms/counters
- Perf canary expansion: tier sweep across models/SKUs
- Explainability endpoint/metadata for Console to display effective config
- Overload protection alignment for cost-efficient tier

## Proposed branch cut + timeline
### Branch cut plan (proposal)
- **Mon 2025-03-10 10:00 PT**: "soft freeze" begins for scheduler/config PRs that impact tier defaults. Only merges with explicit approval from Runtime Scheduling (Sofia) + Release Eng (Connor).
- **Tue 2025-03-11 12:00 PT**: cut `runtime-1.21` release branch.
- **Tue 2025-03-11 EOD**: RC0 build from release branch.
- **Wed 2025-03-12**: staging validation (Hosted + Dedicated canary). If green by EOD: RC1 and begin rollout.

### Freeze rules
After branch cut:
- No new features; only fixes.
- Any changes to tier parameter defaults require:
  1) perf-canary pass (tier sweep job)
  2) at least one staging run for streaming chat route
  3) SRE sign-off on rollback thresholds if metrics/alerts are changed

## Backport policy
### Eligible for backport to runtime-1.21
- P0 correctness/security issues
- Tail-latency regressions attributable to 1.21 changes
- CI/perf canary breakages
- OOM/memory pressure regressions (KV cache pressure limits, compaction thresholds)
- Docs-only changes do not require runtime backport (handled in docs release), unless correcting runtime-facing schema examples in repo

### Not eligible (unless exec escalation)
- "Nice-to-have" tuning improvements (tier parameter re-optimizations without a clear regression)
- New model-family overrides unless required to prevent outages for launch cohort

### Backport validation checklist
- Link original PR + cherry-pick hash
- Unit tests pass
- Perf canary tier sweep pass OR explicit waiver from Sahana + Sofia with rationale logged
- Staging sign-off note in this ticket (include: model, region, route, tier, before/after p95)

## CI stability plan
### Known risk areas
- Perf canary flakes when GPU hosts are saturated (false p95 regressions)
- Streaming cadence regression tests: sensitive to scheduling jitter
- Benchmark-lab runner output occasionally missing tags/labels, breaking report parsing

### Actions
1) Ensure perf-canary jobs for tier sweeps run on reserved CI capacity for release branch (Sahana to coordinate with CI runners).
2) Temporarily increase rerun allowance for "known flaky" tests ONLY on main; release branch should be strict (1 rerun max).
3) Pin perf-canary to a fixed workload corpus revision for 1.21 (avoid moving target during RC).
4) Add a human-readable failure triage template to this ticket for on-call release owner.

### Perf gate for release branch
- Must be within regression thresholds defined by SRE standards:
  - Fast tier: protect p95 and streaming cadence (token interval) first
  - Standard tier: protect p95 and error rates, allow small throughput variance
  - Cost-efficient: protect error rates + timeout/cancel rates; allow p95 increase within tier contract

## Release notes checklist (runtime-1.21)
Owner: Connor (final) + Sahana (technical completeness)

Runtime release notes must include:
- [ ] New config field: `batching_tier` values and defaults; precedence rules (explicit overrides win)
- [ ] Feature flag name + default state (OFF by default; controlled via rollout tooling)
- [ ] Model/route applicability notes (chat/completions/embeddings; streaming caveats)
- [ ] New metrics names + labels (tier/model/route/region) and where to find dashboards
- [ ] Explainability/effective-config endpoint mention (for debugging + Console)
- [ ] Overload protection behavior changes for cost-efficient tier (load shedding reason codes)
- [ ] Known limitations / mitigations (e.g., long-context + high concurrency may trigger stricter admission control)
- [ ] Upgrade notes for Dedicated/Private (schema validation, helm values, migration)

Cross-artifact checklist:
- [ ] Confluence beta release note is ready (Product + DevEx aligned)
- [ ] Docs PR merged / scheduled (SDK examples and FAQ)
- [ ] SRE dashboards/alerts JSON merged and deployed to monitoring env
- [ ] Rollout checklist in Drive finalized and linked from release notes

## Acceptance criteria
- Branch cut executed on agreed date/time and communicated to runtime + SRE + product stakeholders.
- Backport policy documented here and followed for any post-cut changes.
- Release branch CI is stable (no unresolved flakes); perf-canary suite is gating.
- runtime-1.21 release notes are complete with tiered batching items + upgrade notes.
- Rollback owner and criteria confirmed (SRE) prior to enabling any default tier changes.
